newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian financial markets soar on EMU expectations.
newsitem.headline: Italian financial markets soar on EMU expectations.

text.p: Italian stocks and bonds soared to record highs on Wednesday as financial markets were seized by a growing conviction that Italy would be a founder member of a European currency union, planned for launch in 1999.
The heavily-traded September government bond (BTP) futures contract leapt to an all-time high of 136.94 on the London International Financial Futures Exchange (LIFFE).

And an even more closely-watched yield spread between Italian 10-year treasury paper and German bunds narrowed to 92 basis points as investors placed bets that Italy is heading for a close monetary embrace with its northern neighbours.

The spread, which measures the risk premium investors pay for holding Italian bonds, stood at more than tyhree percent less than a year ago, when Italy's chances of joining a first wave of currency union members were still rated as very slim.

The Italian government has made swift progress in restoring order to state accounts and bringing down inflation -- key requirements for EMU membership -- just as France and Germany have run into trouble containing their public sector deficits.

Market watchers are awaiting an audit of French public, finances due on July 21, for a clear indication of how far France is likely to overshoot a three percent deficit-to gross domestic product target this year.

If France looks like it could miss the target -- enshrined in the Maastricht treaty laying down guidelines for currency union membership -- by a wide margin, analysts fear growing calls from some in Germany to delay EMU.
A postponement of EMU, although seen as unlikely, could stop the boom in Italian financial market dead in its tracks.

Milan's bourse also scaled fresh peaks on Wednesday, swept along by a torrent of money from foreign and domestic investors seeking rich pickings as a programme of sell-offs of state assets gathers pace.

The all-share Mibtel index, which tracks all stocks traded on the exchange, hit 13,943 -- its highest level ever -- while the FIB30 September contract, a stock index futures contract based on the top 30 blue chip stocks also rose to record levels.
"Money is pouring in and it looks like we could see a substantial rerating of Italy," said an equities specialist with

"Italy's chances of getting into European monetary union have gone from possible to likely and that is starting to factor into the market," said Anthony Mannara, a share analyst with Milan finance house Milla & Co.

The surge in Italian stocks was also being driven by interest in banks, which are racing to streamline their cumbersome operations to prepare for an onslought from foreign competitors, and in telecom stocks.

State-controlled Telecom Italia and a holding company, Stet, are in the process of being brought together this month in advance of the sale of the merged entity to the public, which is expected later this year.
"The telecommunications companies and the banks together make up the bulk of the stock market's capitalisation," said Mannara.
